name: Quebec nationalism
summary: Quebec nationalism holds that the French-speaking Québécois form a distinct nation whose language, culture and political autonomy must be protected, using the Quebec state as its main instrument. Since the Quiet Revolution it has been a secular, civic and territorial nationalism that ranges from outright independence (Parti Québécois, Bloc Québécois) to autonomist federalism (CAQ), combining French-language laws, laicity rules and a state role in the economy.
scope: Mainstream contemporary Quebec nationalism since the Quiet Revolution, as embodied by René Lévesque's Parti Québécois, the Charter of the French Language, the laicity law and the autonomist CAQ. It excludes the older clerico-nationalism of Lionel Groulx except as history, and fringe ethnic or extremist groups.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The Quiet Revolution made the state the provider of health care and welfare in place of the Church, and mainstream nationalist parties defend that public system.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The PQ is described as centre-left with union ties, so a higher minimum wage fits, though it is not a nationalist demand as such.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Nationalist parties favour a state role in building Francophone economic strength, though the CAQ is business-friendly; the mainstream is a mixed economy.

public-ownership.rationale: The Quiet Revolution's hydroelectric nationalisation and state enterprise were meant to give Francophones control of the economy, and that legacy is still defended.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The PQ is described as centre-left, which implies support for progressive taxation; nationalism itself takes no stand on it.

unions-good.rationale: The PQ has traditionally drawn support from organized labour, though ties are informal.

property-fundamental.rationale: Nationalism has used state intervention and expropriation-style nationalisation for collective goals, so property is not treated as near-absolute; inferred.

regulate-corporations.rationale: State direction of the economy to serve the French-speaking majority, including language rules for business, implies accepting regulation of firms.

cut-welfare.rationale: The welfare state is a Quiet Revolution achievement and part of the national project, although PQ governments have also cut spending at times.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Quebec nationalism has no distinctive stance on surveillance, and the sources do not address it.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not an issue the nationalist tradition addresses; adherents are divided across parties.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Nationalist parties are not distinguished by a position here; supporters of Bill 21 and critics both invoke tolerance.

strong-leader.rationale: The tradition is parliamentary and referendum-based; its charismatic figures such as Lévesque worked through democratic institutions. Inferred.

state-harmful.rationale: Nationalism sees the (Quebec) state as the main tool for national emancipation, so the claim that the state is harmful is rejected.

limit-guns.rationale: Quebec politics has leaned toward stricter gun control, but the sources do not tie this to nationalism; inferred from the party landscape.

empower-police-military.rationale: No stated nationalist position; an independent Quebec's own military was debated among sovereigntists.

decide-locally.rationale: Autonomists and sovereigntists want powers moved from Ottawa to Quebec, but this is about the province, not local communities as such.

rehabilitation.rationale: Quebec's tradition leans toward rehabilitative justice, but this is not stated in the sources; inferred.

traditional-family.rationale: Since the Quiet Revolution secularised society, mainstream nationalism no longer defends Church-based family models, though the older clerical strand did.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Post-Quiet Revolution Quebec is socially liberal and secular, so nationalist parties are broadly supportive; not stated in the sources.

abortion-legal.rationale: Secular modern nationalism accepts legal abortion, in contrast with the earlier clerical strand; inferred.

more-religion-public.rationale: The mainstream stresses laicity, and Bill 21 bars religious symbols for public officials in authority.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Adherents are split, with attention going to national and Indigenous questions more than racial remedies.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed by nationalism, as the sources describe the tradition.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Defending Québécois culture and the French language is the core purpose of the ideology.

gradual-change.rationale: The Quiet Revolution and the sovereignty project sought rapid structural change, but within constitutional and democratic means.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The PQ under St-Pierre Plamondon and the CAQ have called for lower immigration, citing French-language integration capacity.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Sovereigntists want Quebec to take its own place internationally, but the sources give no view on strengthening the UN.

free-trade.rationale: Sovereignty-association was designed to preserve free trade with Canada; the sources give no general position.

nation-first.rationale: Quebec nationalism puts Quebec's interests first relative to Canada, but is not generally hostile to global cooperation.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The sources record no Quebec-nationalist position on this, so it is inferred as neutral.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The sources record no Quebec-nationalist position on this, so it is inferred as neutral.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Not applicable, as the sources describe the tradition.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: The sources record no Quebec-nationalist position on this, so it is inferred as neutral.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: The sources record no Quebec-nationalist position on this, so it is inferred as neutral.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: The sources record no Quebec-nationalist position on this, so it is inferred as neutral.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The sources record no Quebec-nationalist position on this, so it is inferred as neutral.

military-guardian-role.rationale: No strand of Quebec nationalism advocates this; it is foreign to the tradition as the sources describe it.

paid-care-work.rationale: The sources record no Quebec-nationalist position on this, so it is inferred as neutral.

filial-duty.rationale: The sources record no Quebec-nationalist position on this, so it is inferred as neutral.

office-by-exam.rationale: The sources record no Quebec-nationalist position on this, so it is inferred as neutral.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Protecting Quebec head offices from foreign takeover is a recurring nationalist economic aim; inferred.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The sources record no Quebec-nationalist position on this, so it is inferred as neutral.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: The Quebec pension plan was a Quiet Revolution public institution.

land-use-tenure.rationale: No strand of Quebec nationalism advocates this; it is foreign to the tradition as the sources describe it.

worker-ownership.rationale: Labour-aligned supporters may like cooperatives, but collective worker ownership is not a nationalist demand and adherents split.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Nationalists want Quebec's own national history at the centre of teaching, though the sources do not detail curriculum demands; inferred.

single-official-language.rationale: The Charter of the French Language makes French the language of schooling, signage and business, the movement's signature policy.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred: Quebec has restricted farmland purchases by non-residents, but nationalists mostly focus on language and autonomy and the issue is not part of the doctrine.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred: mainstream Quebec nationalism stresses civic equality under a common secular framework and resists group-based remedies, as seen in the laicity law's uniform rules.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred: the centre-left PQ has some anti-consumerist currents but the nationalist doctrine has no stated view on consumer culture.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred: the movement pursues sovereignty through referendums and legal means and has no tradition of backing foreign armed groups.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The movement is built on a people's right to self-determination, including leaving a union by referendum, so forced intervention to hold a member in is rejected.

corporate-influence.rationale: Inferred from the social-democratic, state-interventionist tilt of Quebec nationalism and its Quiet Revolution roots; Quebec has repeatedly tightened lobbying and party-financing rules.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from the aim of shielding Quebec self-determination from outside interference; Quebec sovereigntists backed limits on outside referendum spending.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred from the nationalist concern with demographic survival of the French-speaking nation; Quebec has long run family-support policies.

residents-only-property.rationale: Adherents are split; the concern for protecting the nation is not clearly tied to local property restrictions, so this is inferred as neutral.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred from a state-active social-democratic tendency, but the nationalist parties have no job-guarantee programme and adherents are split.

democratic-peace.rationale: Inferred from the civic, liberal-democratic character of contemporary Quebec nationalism; it holds democracy is best and does not make this a defining claim.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Inferred from the civic nationalism that grounds the Quebec state in democratic legitimacy and rule of law, including enforcing its own language and laicity laws.

non-intervention.rationale: Sovereigntists want Quebec independence and its own voice abroad, but have no settled doctrine on intervention in other states; inferred as neutral.

industrial-unions.rationale: Quebec labour movement is close to nationalism, but craft versus industry organisation is not a nationalist issue.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Contemporary Quebec nationalism is civic and territorial, and mainstream parties reject ethnic-conspiracy claims; this is inferred from that civic character.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred from the secular, modern outlook after the Quiet Revolution, but mainstream parties have not proposed abolishing legal marriage.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Quebec has a strong access-to-information regime and the nationalist parties, who built the modern Quebec state, support transparency; inferred from that.

local-production.rationale: Inferred from the nationalist emphasis on economic self-reliance and state support for local firms and farming.

informal-organisation.rationale: The Parti Québécois and Bloc Québécois are permanent parties and the movement is organised through parties and unions, so informal small-group organising is rejected.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The cited sources do not address international law. Sovereigntists invoke the international right of self-determination against Canada's courts, while Quebec governments have shielded the laicity law from rights review; the two pull in opposite directions, so 0 at low confidence.

religious-nation.rationale: Contemporary Quebec nationalism is secular and the laicity law separates state from religion; the nation is defined by language and culture, not religion.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Sovereigntists seek equal standing for Quebec among nations, not a subordinate rank; inferred, as the idea of ritual tribute is not addressed.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Sovereigntists argue Quebec's taxes should be spent by Quebec rather than in Ottawa-run transfers; inferred from the case for a sovereign Quebec.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The PQ is described as centre-left, not as seeking common ownership of the means of production; inferred.

defeat-communism.rationale: Quebec nationalism has no anti-communist crusade; it is a social-democratic, nation-focused movement, so this is inferred.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Quebec's system mixes the public network with subsidised private and independent providers, and the CAQ extends that; inferred, not a core nationalist demand.

religion-illusion.rationale: The laicity law separates state and religion but does not claim religion is an illusion that will fade; inferred.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The Quiet Revolution aimed to make francophones 'masters in their own house' within a market economy, not to replace it; inferred.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The PQ's feminism works mainly through law and public programmes within the existing economy; inferred.

socialized-care.rationale: The Quiet Revolution state took over care once run by the Church and funds public childcare; inferred, as not a nationalist demand as such.

purge-loanwords.rationale: The Charter of the French Language protects French but promotes it through schooling and commerce rules, not a purge of loanwords; inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: Nationalist parties recognise Indigenous nations and agreements such as the James Bay treaty; inferred from the PQ platform.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Quebec nationalism is built around the nation-state and the Quebec state, not communal property; inferred.

majority-settlement.rationale: Quebec nationalism seeks to protect the majority francophones in their own territory, not to settle the majority in minority regions; inferred.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Adherents favour a mixed, state-assisted economy but do not frame it as a third way; contested and inferred.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Inferred: Quebec nationalism bases its claim on the French-speaking nation's long presence and language, but the civic form stresses the territory's residents of all origins and also recognizes Indigenous nations.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Mainstream civic Quebec nationalism since the Quiet Revolution rejects ethnic extremism and nothing in the sources supports denial; inferred from its civic character.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Quiet Revolution Quebec is secular and liberal on this issue; the PQ and Quebec state have long protected gay rights, and the Charter's era broke with clerical morality.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The movement works through elections and referendums, and the sources show it as a democratic one.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The laicity law enforces state neutrality toward religion and the Quiet Revolution ended the Church's role in the state, so the state punishing blasphemy is the opposite of its stance.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Inferred: Quebec nationalists see Quebec as itself having been subordinated within Canada, so they oppose a metropole-serving colonial order, though the sources do not address overseas territories.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Inferred: a religious duty of armed resistance is foreign to this secular nationalism, which rejects violence and seeks independence by referendum.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: The laicity law makes the state religiously neutral, and the nationalism is secular and democratic, so removing rulers by force for not following religious law contradicts it.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Inferred: the movement relies on referendums and popular consultation and the PQ promotes citizen participation, but direct decision-making in workplaces and universities is not a stated aim.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Inferred: the sources do not address it and nationalists are split, with some on the left adopting it and others stressing language and nation first.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred: Quebec has legislated protections for gender identity and the nationalist mainstream has generally not opposed them, but it is not a nationalist theme in the sources.

assisted-dying.rationale: Quebec's National Assembly passed the first provincial medical aid in dying law in 2014, with broad cross-party support including PQ members, so the nationalist mainstream backs it.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Inferred: the nationalist movement includes left and right wings and sometimes presents the national question as above that divide, but the sources show no consensus on it.

alienated-labor.rationale: Inferred: the PQ is social-democratic in origin but the sources do not frame work through alienation.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Inferred: the laicity law is aimed at religious symbols generally and mainstream nationalists officially reject targeting Islam, though some supporters make the claim.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The Act respecting the laicity of the State establishes the state's separation from religion, and Quiet Revolution nationalism replaced clerical authority with popular sovereignty.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: The laicity law (s5) bars public officials in positions of authority, and teachers, from wearing religious symbols at work, and the nationalist mainstream backs it. It does not cover students, so the statement is only partly matched.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Inferred: Quebec nationalism is not opposed to such worker protections, but the sources do not address it.

social-market-economy.rationale: Quebec nationalism combines a state role in the economy since the Quiet Revolution with a market economy, which fits a mixed economy with social protection.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Inferred: sovereigntists have usually planned a Quebec army or joint defence in an independent Quebec, so abolition is not the position, though the sources do not address it.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred: the movement's state-led, social-democratic tradition favors broad benefit over letting some groups get rich first.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Inferred: sovereigntist parties have generally planned to keep NATO and NORAD ties, while others favor neutrality, so adherents are split.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Modern Quebec nationalism is a democratic, civic movement working through elected institutions, with no role for hereditary rule.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Inferred from the Quebec tradition of cooperative finance and the state-led economic model of the Quiet Revolution; no such scheme is stated in the sources.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: The sources do not address it, and nationalist parties range from social democratic to fiscally conservative autonomists.

property-franchise.rationale: Civic nationalism rests on universal citizenship and democratic sovereignty of the Quebec people.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Inferred from the Parti Québécois's social-democratic and progressive lineage; the specific thesis is not stated.

reification.rationale: A Marxist theory of commodity relations is not part of mainstream Quebec nationalism; inferred from its social-democratic rather than Marxist character.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred from the left-leaning Parti Québécois tradition, which is sceptical of concentrated private power; not stated.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The movement works through statutes such as the Charter of the French Language and the laicity law, passed openly in the National Assembly under the rule of law.

racial-franchise.rationale: Since the Quiet Revolution the movement is civic and territorial, open to all residents regardless of ancestry.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the movement's emphasis on democratic participation and referendums.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred from the democratic, accountable-government stance of the mainstream parties; no policy is stated.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The laicity law makes the state secular and neutral between religions, which is incompatible with legal restrictions on interfaith marriage.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Civic, secular nationalism opposes targeting religious minorities; the laicity framework is about state neutrality, not private boycotts.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Inferred: the Quebec state has run citizen consultations and Parti Québécois governments favored participatory democracy, but lot-selected assemblies are not a defining nationalist position.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Inferred: Quiet Revolution secularism and the laicity law treat religion as a private matter to be modernized, not bound by clerical authority; the law does not address doctrine itself.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Inferred from the Parti Québécois's centre-left, union-linked outlook; concentration of wealth is not a nationalist theme as such.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred: the secular, civic nationalism since the Quiet Revolution is socially liberal, though the question is not a nationalist theme.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The laicity law keeps the state neutral and secular, not atheistic, and does not promote atheism in schools.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Inferred: the nationalist parties run Quebec's own police and justice system and favour firmer law enforcement, not abolition.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Adherents split: Quebec nationalism seeks recognition of a distinct nation within Canada, but is not discussed as a consociational model.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The Quiet Revolution moved welfare from the Church to the state, and the mainstream parties defend that public role over charity.

term-limits.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; no source shows a common position on term limits.

vote-delegation.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; nothing in the sources discusses delegated voting.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's concerns are language, culture and autonomy, so adherents are indifferent.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred: the secular Quiet Revolution outlook favours equality of women, though religious institutions' internal rules lie outside the movement's scope.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The Quiet Revolution era reforms established spousal equality in Quebec's civil law, which mainstream nationalist parties support.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Quebec nationalism stresses a civic Québécois citizenry built around French; nothing in the sources endorses non-citizen voting, so this is inferred from its emphasis on common citizenship and integration.

rent-control.rationale: Not a theme in the sources; inferred from the Quiet Revolution's interventionist, social-democratic state and the PQ's left-of-centre tradition.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from mainstream nationalists' defence of Quebec's cultural industries and creators, which rely on copyright.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Mainstream Quebec nationalism since the Quiet Revolution is a secular, civic, democratic movement with no tradition of drilled national-service youth movements.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Not a stated theme; inferred from the sovereigntist, broadly left-leaning movement's reluctance toward nuclear militarism.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; sovereigntists stress independence but have accepted NATO and NORAD membership for an independent Quebec, so adherents are split.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Not a defining issue; inferred from the movement's own politics of historical memory and recognition of peoples, though adherents are not unanimous.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the PQ's social-democratic orientation and state role in the economy, not from a stated principle.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Nothing in the movement suggests absolute pacifism; it is a mainstream democratic movement that accepts ordinary legal self-defence.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Modern Quebec nationalism dates the nation from New France and the Quiet Revolution rather than antiquity and is civic in character; inferred from that, as the sources do not address ancient continuity.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Not addressed; Quebec nationalists are split on this, and the movement as such takes no position.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; adherents are divided and it has no stated position on feminist theory.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The Quiet Revolution secularised Quebec nationalism and the laicity law keeps the state religiously neutral, so it does not sanctify the national dead; the Patriotes are commemorated in a civic way.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Post-Quiet-Revolution nationalism is secular and framed in terms of language, democracy and interests, and the laicity law separates state and religion.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The movement aims to protect French in a Quebec territory and to have the nation live there, not to be a centre for a diaspora; inferred from its territorial focus.

culture-before-state.rationale: Sovereigntists treat the state as the main instrument for protecting language and culture, as with the Charter of the French Language, rather than waiting for cultural renewal first.

god-not-male.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is secular and takes no position on religious language.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Not addressed; secular nationalism takes no stance on religious texts beyond keeping them out of state life.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The movement has sought francophone advancement in business (the 'Maîtres chez nous' era) but frames this as equal opportunity, not reserving economic life for the majority; inferred.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Quebec nationalists are mainly concerned with the Quebec territory as a whole; the sources do not address merging regions, so adherents have no clear position.

independent-unions.rationale: Inferred from the Quiet Revolution's strong union ties and the PQ's centre-left, union-linked base.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The ideology has no stated position on this, and adherents are split, so it is left neutral.

local-essentials-public.rationale: The Quiet Revolution made the state, not the Church or private owners, the provider of health, welfare and hydro power, and nationalist parties defend this.

second-chamber.rationale: Inferred: Quebec abolished its Legislative Council in 1968 and the movement has not sought a second chamber; this is not a nationalist doctrine as such.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred: the movement relies on the Quebec state as its main instrument, not local community ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The ideology has no stated position on this, and adherents are split, so it is left neutral.

family-wage.rationale: The ideology has no stated position on this, and adherents are split, so it is left neutral.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: The ideology has no stated position on this, and adherents are split, so it is left neutral.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: The ideology has no stated position on this, and adherents are split, so it is left neutral.

anonymous-payments.rationale: The ideology has no stated position on this, and adherents are split, so it is left neutral.

online-anonymity.rationale: The ideology has no stated position on this, and adherents are split, so it is left neutral.

person-over-state.rationale: The ideology has no stated position on this, and adherents are split, so it is left neutral.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Post-Quiet-Revolution nationalism is secular and defends laicity rules, so it does not frame politics as serving a spiritual nature.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Quebec nationalists seek autonomy or sovereignty entrenched against Ottawa, so revocable powers would defeat their aim.

gm-crops.rationale: The ideology has no stated position on this, and adherents are split, so it is left neutral.

dense-cities.rationale: The ideology has no stated position on this, and adherents are split, so it is left neutral.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Mainstream Quebec nationalism is civic and territorial, not racial, and defines the nation by language and culture.

racial-pride.rationale: The ideology has no stated position on this, and adherents are split, so it is left neutral.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The movement is peaceful and electoral and has no stated military doctrine, so adherents are not clearly aligned.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Quebec nationalism makes French the core of Quebec identity, but since the Quiet Revolution it is a territorial and civic nationalism that does not link Quebec to francophones elsewhere across borders.

communal-electorates.rationale: Modern Quebec nationalism is civic and secular and the laicity law keeps religion out of public life, so religiously separate electorates are contrary to it.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Inferred: sovereigntists see Canadian federal institutions as a constraint but do not claim foreign powers plot against Quebec.

free-public-college.rationale: Quebec has the lowest tuition in Canada, a legacy of the Quiet Revolution, and the movement has supported free or near-free education, but it is not a core platform item.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred: Quebec runs a cap-and-trade carbon market and nationalist parties back it, but pollution taxes as such are not a defining stance.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred: the PQ case for independence appeals to the future of the nation, and the party backs environmental protection, but this is not a stated principle.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Inferred: the movement stresses gender equality as a Quebec value, not distinct feminine values.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred: sovereigntist parties favour an independent Quebec with a modest defence and Quebec's public opinion is more pacifist than Canada's, but it is not a stated platform.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred: sovereigntists criticise federal negotiations as opaque and promise referendums on treaties and sovereignty, but diplomacy is not a core theme.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred: the PQ proposes an open, trading independent Quebec in an economic association with Canada, which implies free capital movement.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred: mainstream post-Quiet-Revolution nationalism is civic and constitutional; armed groups like the FLQ are repudiated.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Not addressed; Quebec nationalism has anti-conscription history but no doctrine of refusing orders. Split.

collective-bargaining.rationale: The Quiet Revolution aligned nationalism with a strong union movement and social-democratic policy, as in the Parti Québécois tradition.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred: Quebec governments use work premiums and family tax measures within a state-active social model; not a stated nationalist demand.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Quebec has a balanced-budget law, but nationalist parties differ on fiscal rules; not a stated nationalist position.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Not addressed; Quebec nationalism is focused on language and autonomy rather than the global economic order.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Mainstream Quebec nationalism pursues sovereignty by referendum and uses the Quebec state as its main instrument, rejecting smashing it.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred: nationalism here centres on a single national community with a state-led economic model, not open-ended experiment.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Not stated; hydro-electric nationalisation is a national resource symbol, but no stance on natural capital accounting.

sacred-nation.rationale: Post-Quiet-Revolution Quebec nationalism is secular, civic and territorial, so describing the nation as sacred does not fit.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Quebec nationalists backed low tuition in the 2012 student protests, but debt cancellation is not a stated position.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred: nationalist writers have compared French Canadians to a colonised people (as in Pierre Vallières), but mainstream parties rarely use it.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Not addressed; mainstream nationalism stresses cultural particularity without a stated view on human nature.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred: the nationalist project backs public French-language culture and broadcasting such as Radio-Canada and Télé-Québec; not stated in the sources.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Contemporary Quebec nationalism is secular and laicist, so it does not hold that all religions share one truth; inferred from the laicity law.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred: the Quebec state has a long role in supporting agriculture and the nationalist parties defend supply management, but this is not a defining position.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Quebec nationalist parties and the Bloc have supported nuclear disarmament; this is a documented but secondary position, inferred from their platforms.

workers-own-party.rationale: The Parti Québécois is a broad-based national party and the movement holds no unified view on a separate workers' party.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from the movement's secular, civic and rights-based outlook; not specifically addressed.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from the movement's civic equality principles and the Quebec Charter of rights; not specifically addressed.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Quebec nationalists define French as a distinct national language but have no stated view on how others name languages.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: No stated position; mainstream nationalists favour state regulation, which cuts against a tort-only model.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from the secular, civic and democratic outlook; no role for chiefs in Quebec law is stated.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is split between environmental commitment and liberty concerns.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between social-democratic and conservative views on sentencing.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: The Charter of the French Language makes French the common public language, and nationalists favour newcomers learning it and integrating into the French-speaking nation.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Quebec nationalism is closely tied to its strong union movement and the Parti Québécois's labour-friendly platform, which opposes right-to-work rules; Quebec also has the Rand formula.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred: voter ID is not a theme, and Quebec law already requires ID at polling places; adherents are not split along nationalist lines on it.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The laicity law requires the state to be neutral and not favour any religion, which implies no interpretation has legal precedence, though the law itself is contested for restricting religious symbols.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Nationalists treat democratic self-determination by referendum and election as the legitimate route, and the movement defends its procedures as democratic, though it also pursues policies such as language rules.

premarital-sex.rationale: The Quiet Revolution secularised Quebec society and ended the Church's moral authority, so mainstream nationalists accept sex outside marriage.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred: Quebec nationalists are civil libertarians on democratic grounds and have never advocated internet shutdowns, but the issue is not addressed.

negative-income-tax.rationale: The Quebec state-centred model defends public welfare and social programs, so nationalist parties would not replace welfare with a negative income tax.

women-suffrage.rationale: Women's suffrage in Quebec came in 1940, and modern nationalist parties embrace equality of rights as a basic value of Quebec society.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred: the secular, laicist nationalism that grew from the Quiet Revolution, which broke the Church's hold, views Catholic-era norms as having restrained women, but this is not stated.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred: Quebec civic nationalism rejects ethnic definitions of the nation, so mainstream adherents accept the social-construct view, but the sources do not discuss race.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Quebec has a dedicated Secrétariat à la condition féminine and Conseil du statut de la femme, created in the post-Quiet Revolution state-building era, and the nationalist parties defend them.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the Quiet Revolution's social-democratic, state-led economy; property in unowned resources is not discussed.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from the movement's civic, internationalist outlook and wish for Quebec to join international bodies as a state; not stated directly.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred from the secular laicity framework, which keeps religion out of the state; scripture literalism is not addressed.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from the Quiet Revolution's secular modernism and the wide acceptance of gender equality in Quebec politics.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred from the movement's democratic, market-and-state economy; a bureaucratic planned state would not be a cause for it.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred from the sovereigntist call for referendums and direct democracy on the national question.

national-church-status.rationale: The laicity law bars religious privilege in the state, so a national church with a special legal status is rejected.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Quebec nationalism itself claims territorial autonomy for the French-speaking majority region within Canada, so adherents agree with the principle.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: The movement's route to sovereignty is a referendum in which Quebec's inhabitants decide for themselves.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred from the sovereignty project, which would redraw the Canadian federation's borders by a vote rather than keep them fixed.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred from a modern, urban, consumer-oriented society; no source addresses simple living.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred from the civic, territorial nationalism, which emphasises a shared French-language civic identity rather than settlement limits.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred from secular egalitarian values; conscription is a historical sore point (1917, 1944) and gender equality is widely held.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Modern Quebec nationalism is civic and secular, and the sources do not frame the tie to land as spiritual; adherents split.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Inferred: a secular, civic and social-democratic nationalism is committed to due process; the issue is not addressed.

close-ties-china.rationale: Not addressed; Quebec nationalism has no distinct line on China.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: The movement defends French in Quebec and links to the Francophonie, but does not set a general kin-minority policy; inferred as split.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: The PQ is centre-left, but resource ownership by all is not a stated theme; strands split.

self-ownership.rationale: Not addressed; adherents range across centre-left and centre-right.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Taxation of consumption is not a nationalist issue; parties differ.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Inferred from the centre-left, union-linked PQ and the Quiet Revolution's universal public services.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Inferred: the PQ is a party with union ties and works through parties and institutions, opposing leader-to-people rule.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred from the centre-left PQ's tradition of regulating the economy; not a stated theme.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: The laicity law and the Quiet Revolution's break from Church-run politics support cutting politics across, and apart from, religious lines.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Quebec nationalism combines modernity with preserving French culture, but not archaic ancestral values; adherents split.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred from the secular, post-Quiet Revolution outlook and gender equality in Quebec law; not explicitly discussed.

national-resource-control.rationale: Inferred from the state-centred economy described in the overview, such as public hydroelectric power.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Quebec nationalism is not organised around a theory of distributive justice, and the movement is centre-left in practice; adherents are not aligned.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: The Parti Québécois and CAQ take no common stance on a financial transactions tax; inferred.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Quebec nationalists generally frame the main obstacle as language and national status, and take no common line on racial disadvantage.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: The nationalist parties hold that Quebec's own legitimate procedure sets its laws, and their language and laicity laws rely on legal process; inferred.

automate-paid-work.rationale: The movement has no position on automating paid work.

multipolar-world.rationale: Quebec nationalism seeks national self-determination within the existing order, not a multipolar world as such; adherents are not aligned.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: The social-democratic wing of the movement is not Marxist and the mainstream parties do not hold this theory; inferred.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: The Parti Québécois joined national feeling to social-democratic policy for ordinary Quebecers; inferred from its record.

material-over-identity.rationale: Quebec nationalism puts language and cultural identity at the centre of its politics, ahead of narrowly material demands.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Quebec nationalists work within a multiparty liberal democracy and reject one-party communist rule; inferred.

missingStatements.text: A state may require one language to be the common language of schooling, work and commerce, even where this restricts the use of other languages.
missingStatements.rationale: The Charter of the French Language makes French the language of instruction, signage and business, the movement's signature policy.

missingStatements.text: A region's secession should be subject to conditions set by the national parliament, such as a clear question and a clear majority.
missingStatements.rationale: Sovereigntists consider the Clarity Act illegitimate and hold that Quebec alone should set the terms of secession.

missingStatements.text: Public employees in positions of authority should be barred from wearing religious symbols at work.
missingStatements.rationale: The 2019 laicity law bans such symbols for judges, police and teachers, and the nationalist parties support it.

notes: Parties differ: the PQ and Bloc seek independence, the CAQ is autonomist; the older clerical strand and Bill 21's critics within the movement would answer religion and family statements differently. Many answers are low-confidence inferences from the secular, centre-left post-1960 mainstream.
